questiontext.text:
A farmer wants to calculate the area of a rectangular maize plot in order to determine the correct amount of fertilizer needed. Using a precision measuring tape, the length of the plot is recorded as \({@plot_length_disp@}\) m (correct to \({@length_dp@}\) decimal place(s)) and the width as \({@plot_width_disp@}\) m (correct to \({@width_dp@}\) decimal place(s)). Find:

(a) The absolute error in the area of the plot.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) The relative error in the area of the plot.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(c) The percentage error in the area of the plot.

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
The plot length was recorded as \({@plot_length_disp@}\) m, correct to \({@length_dp@}\) decimal place(s), and the width as \({@plot_width_disp@}\) m, correct to \({@width_dp@}\) decimal place(s).

Absolute errors in the individual measurements:

Since the length is correct to \({@length_dp@}\) decimal place(s), its absolute error is half the smallest unit:

\[ \text{Length error} = \frac{1}{2 \times {@length_scale@}} = {@plot_length_err@} \text{ m} \]

Similarly, since the width is correct to \({@width_dp@}\) decimal place(s):

\[ \text{Width error} = \frac{1}{2 \times {@width_scale@}} = {@plot_width_err@} \text{ m} \]

(a) Absolute error in the area:

Using the recorded measurements:

\[ \text{Working area} = {@plot_length_disp@} \times {@plot_width_disp@} = {@W_plot_area@} \text{ m}^2 \]

Using the maximum possible length and width:

\[ \text{Max length} = {@plot_length_disp@} + {@plot_length_err@} = {@max_plot_length@} \text{ m} \]

\[ \text{Max width} = {@plot_width_disp@} + {@plot_width_err@} = {@max_plot_width@} \text{ m} \]

\[ \text{Maximum area} = {@max_plot_length@} \times {@max_plot_width@} = {@max_plot_area@} \text{ m}^2 \]

\[ \text{Absolute error} = \text{Maximum area} - \text{Working area} = {@max_plot_area@} - {@W_plot_area@} = {@ta1@} \text{ m}^2 \]

(b) Relative error:

\[ \text{Relative error} = \frac{\text{Absolute error}}{\text{Working area}} = \frac{{@ta1@}}{{@W_plot_area@}} \approx {@ta2@} \]

(c) Percentage error:

\[ \text{Percentage error} = \text{Relative error} \times 100\% = {@ta2@} \times 100\% \approx {@ta3@}\% \]
